key_insight: A compact mesh-free Kolmogorov--Arnold PINN with learnable edge functions and staged optimization can accurately solve the biharmonic equation without meshing or auxiliary variables.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical high-order PDE solver for thin-plate and other fourth-order boundary-value problems where mesh generation and stiff optimization are major bottlenecks.
method: KAN edges use learnable univariate functions parameterized by radial basis functions.
High-order differentiability is maintained with tanh activations and a normalized residual loss.
Training is automated with AdamW followed by L-BFGS plus hill-climbing search for penalty and schedule tuning.
evidence_signal: On a manufactured unit-square benchmark, the model reached a relative L2 error of 1.593×10^-5 and training loss of 3.065×10^-6 using 7,801 trainable parameters, with more than 150× error reduction across iterations.
watch_item: Performance is shown on a smooth benchmark, so robustness to irregular geometries, noisy data, and harder real-world biharmonic cases still needs validation.
paper_title: Mesh-Free Numerical Approximation of the Biharmonic Equation via Optimized Kolmogorov--Arnold Neural Networks
